name: MIT App Inventor
type: web-based visual programming environment / mobile application development environment

programming_model.interaction: programs are constructed by assembling interlocking blocks

educational_purpose: transition from technology consumption to technology creation
core_idea: Learners construct functional mobile applications by visually composing programming blocks and connecting them to interface components, events, data, and device capabilities.
feedback_loop: Learners can run and test their application on a connected phone, tablet, Chromebook, or emulator while developing it.
papert_relevance: The learner works with a personally meaningful computational artifact—a functioning mobile application—and can iteratively construct, execute, inspect, debug, and modify it. Programming concepts are encountered through the construction of an external artifact rather than being presented solely as abstract syntax.
object_to_think_with: A functioning mobile application and its constituent interactive components

source_notes.official_description: MIT describes App Inventor as an intuitive visual programming environment for building fully functional apps for smartphones and tablets.
source_notes.official_software_status: MIT explicitly describes App Inventor as an open-source tool.
source_notes.official_software_license: The appinventor-sources repository contains the Apache License 2.0.
source_notes.official_content_license: The MIT App Inventor website states that its work is licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0.
source_notes.official_cost: MIT describes App Inventor as a free web-based platform.
